claim.quote: Observation of a neutrino burst from the supernova SN1987A

date.note: The burst itself was recorded on 23 February 1987 (see key_value_text); that is the observation date, not a publication or announcement date. No earlier public announcement date could be read from a fetched page.

key_value_text.quote: A neutrino burst was observed in the Kamiokande II detector on 23 February, 7:35:35 UT (+-1 min) during a time interval of 13 sec.
key_value_text.value: A neutrino burst of 13-second duration observed in the Kamiokande-II detector on 23 February 1987, 7:35:35 UT (± 1 min).

name: Kamiokande-II observation of SN 1987A neutrinos
notes: 2026-09-17: result_type changed from first_detection to observation to match the publication title ("Observation of a neutrino burst..."), per A16. 2026-10-25 audit: the "first detection" wording was removed from the summary because none of the cited pages states it for this paper; `date` now holds the PRL publication date (the burst itself was recorded on 23 February 1987).

official_url.note: No official experiment result page carries a URL for this 1987 paper in the sources fetched; only the journal DOI record is available.

summary.plain: In February 1987 the Kamiokande II detector recorded a burst of neutrinos: 11 electron events with energies from 7.5 to 36 MeV over about 13 seconds, the first two pointing back toward the Large Magellanic Cloud, where supernova SN 1987A had appeared.
summary.technical: Kamiokande-II recorded a neutrino burst on 23 February 1987, 7:35:35 UT (±1 min), during a time interval of 13 s: 11 electron events of energy 7.5 to 36 MeV, of which the first two point back to the Large Magellanic Cloud with angles 18° ± 18° and 15° ± 27°. The paper title attributes the burst to supernova SN 1987A.

title: Observation of a neutrino burst from the supernova SN1987A
why_it_matters: Kamiokande's own history page calls the February 1987 detection of supernova neutrinos in the Large Magellanic Cloud a major breakthrough. A 2018 IceCube abstract notes that individual astrophysical sources previously detected in neutrinos are limited to the Sun and the supernova 1987A.
